Test whether a bamboo-forest aerial duel reads through opposed body arcs, one sword-contact point, and distinct landing anchors inside a complex misty ravine scene, with the attachment used only for one adult lead's visible appearance.

Create a cinematic wuxia action photograph of two complete, unmistakably adult swordswomen suspended inside a misty bamboo ravine at dawn. The lead visibly follows the supplied portrait through long near-black wavy hair with a center part, a softly oval face, warm brown eyes, straight brows, and natural closed lips. Show a bamboo-forest aerial duel across three depth layers: foreground leaves, the fighters above a silver stream, and receding green trunks. The lead cuts downward from camera right while the rival rises from camera left; their full-body arcs oppose each other and their blades meet at one crisp, readable steel contact point. Below them, a mossed boulder is the lead's landing anchor and an arched root shelf is the rival's separate landing anchor. A fallen red paper umbrella turns in the stream. Prioritize anatomical completeness, separated silhouettes, exchange geometry, and spatially plausible descent. Use a 50 mm lateral view, pale dawn backlight, suspended mist droplets, restrained robe motion, sharp faces, and photoreal bamboo, water, steel, and cloth.
